title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 46-48: a set S with a topology τ, split into a closed part T and its open complement U = S\T. In the poset ('ultratopological', Alexandrov) case S is an ordered set and topologies correspond to order relations. On T one is given a new topology τ'_0, which must be finer than τ|T for the argument to work. One defines a modified topology τ' on S, 'property (b)': a set X is τ'-closed iff
1° X∩U is closed in U for τ|U;
2° X∩T is closed in T for τ'_0;
3° the τ-closure of X_U = X∩U, intersected with T, lies in X∩T.

This is a recollement: keep τ on the open stratum, replace the topology of the closed stratum, and require closed sets to contain the old τ-limit points from U. In the poset picture, relations are deleted inside T while relations between U and T are kept.

Property e) to be proved is a characterization of τ'. Any τ'' satisfying
(i) τ'' ≤ τ (here ≤ must mean 'finer', i.e. more closed sets),
(ii) τ''|T = τ'_0,
(iii) τ''|U = τ|U,
(iv) a τ''-closed X with X∩T τ-closed is τ-closed
should equal τ'. The marginal gloss on (iv) says that τ is the topology induced through id: (S,τ'') → (S,τ) relative to T.

Grothendieck notes that (i)-(iii) already give one comparison of τ'' with τ'. For the converse, a τ''-closed X trivially satisfies 1° by (iii) and 2° by (ii). Condition 3° is the crux: one needs cl_τ(X_U) ⊂ cl_τ''(X_U) ⊂ X. He reduces this to an 'annex question': is cl_τ''(A) = cl_τ(A) for all A ⊂ U, i.e. is the τ''-closure of a subset of U automatically τ-closed?

A margin note added later, 'mais c'est faux!!', flags the proposed characterization as false. Page 48 confirms this with a small poset counterexample (I' with three elements, A = {b}). It then replaces (iv) by the evident condition: for A ⊂ U the τ- and τ'-closures coincide. This yields the closure formula cl_τ'(A) = cl_τ(A∩U) ∪ cl_{τ'_0}(A∩T). The formula is consistent because cl_τ(A∩U)∩T is τ-closed, hence τ'_0-closed when τ'_0 is finer than τ|T.

Purpose: a lemma in the 'algebra of figures' / poset-topology chapter. It lets one modify finite (ultra)topologies stratum by stratum, presumably for the homotopy-invariance corollaries of p. 46 (a map that is homotopically proper with weakly contractible fibres gives an isomorphism, a Quillen Theorem A analogue for posets).
errors: The characterization (i)-(iv) attempted on this page is false, as Grothendieck himself notes in the margin ('mais c'est faux!!') and shows on p.48 with a counterexample. Condition (iv) does not force closures of subsets of U to agree.

The order convention is ambiguous. For 3° to be non-automatic and the argument to make sense, '≤' must mean 'finer' (more closed sets). Under the coarser reading, 3° would follow trivially from cl_τ ⊂ cl_τ''.
The machine transcription's '(U = T\S)' should read U = S\T (complement of the closed part T), as on p.48.

ideas.what: Modifying a topology on a closed subset T while keeping it on the open complement U, with closed sets characterized by three gluing conditions
ideas.modern_name: Recollement / gluing of topologies along an open-closed decomposition; in the poset case, deleting order relations on a down-closed or up-closed subset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Alexandrov spaces; the recollement formalism of Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne for sheaves)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the sheaf-theoretic recollement idea is in SGA4 (open/closed decomposition).

ideas.what: Characterizing the modified topology by restriction conditions plus agreement of closures of subsets of the open part, giving the explicit closure formula cl_τ'(A) = cl_τ(A∩U) ∪ cl_{τ'_0}(A∩T)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine point-set lemma about gluing topologies on an open/closed decomposition, with a self-corrected false characterization. Of interest only as a glimpse of Grothendieck's 1986 work on finite/ultratopological 'figures', not as new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '(U = T\S)' should be read as U = S\T (complement of T in S).
The margin note at top left reads 'mais c'est faux!!', added next to 'Caractérisation par les conditions dites'.
In 3°, X_U denotes X∩U; the first closure is with respect to τ: cl^{(τ)}(X_U) ∩ T ⊂ X∩T.
'τ'' sur 𝔛 [?]' is likely 'τ'' sur S'.
